title: Roy Eldridge as jam-session leader and a giant of the trumpet
summary: Wilson praises Roy Eldridge's pure jazz feeling, ranking him after Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Of course, one of the great spearheads of the jam sessions was Roy Eldridge -- he just loved to play, and find these trumpet players and blast them out in these different towns.
There's never enough said about Roy. He was a pioneer.
Oh, right. Roy Eldridge is one of the giants -- after Armstrong, I'd say.
He came through Milwaukee, Chicago, the whole area, man. Roy Eldridge.
He had that pure jazz feeling in his trumpet.
The essence of the jazz rhythm, just like in Armstrong, is in Roy.
Sure is nice to hear Dizzy say that, too.
Well, Dizzy, I'm sure, as a young fellow -- he recognized that in Roy, too.

And that's still there, too; I hear it once in awhile. It's real, like Armstrong, it's not to be confused with any music of other countries. It's American jazz, purely, that comes out of that trumpet.
